candidates.tagline: Roku launched a 24/7 AI slop channel. Characters don't blink. Arrows travel backwards.
candidates.story: In August 2026, Roku quietly added 'Fairground AI' — a free channel broadcasting AI-generated content 24 hours a day, interrupted only by AI-generated ads — promising 'gorgeous things' and delivering medieval soldiers with frozen eyes, backwards physics, and cosmic octopuses attacking cities.
candidates.why_funny: The world's most confident description of AI content as 'gorgeous' is now a 24/7 monument to everything AI video gets wrong.
candidates.alt: Futurism article thumbnail showing Roku's Fairground AI channel — a collage of AI-generated scenes including blurry cinematic landscapes and uncanny figures, with the Futurism logo and the headline 'Roku Unleashes 24/7 AI Slop Channel'

candidates.tagline: Edinburgh's North Bridge: closed 8 years for works, reopened with exactly zero cycle lanes.
candidates.story: Edinburgh's North Bridge closed in 2018 for major refurbishment, with plans to create a cycling and public transport corridor; it fully reopened on July 31, 2026 — after eight years — with no cycling infrastructure whatsoever, just regular car lanes, leaving cyclists to navigate around one of the city's busiest crossings exactly as before.
candidates.why_funny: Eight years of Edinburgh telling cyclists 'we're working on it' culminated in a grand unveiling of: a road.
candidates.alt: Edinburgh North Bridge viewed from street level, showing the grand Victorian stone bridge carrying car traffic across a deep valley, with no cycle lanes or cycling infrastructure visible
